description.narrative: (Ghana): This activity will strengthen access, demand, and uptake of high-impact health products related to family planning (FP); maternal, newborn, child health and nutrition (MNCHN); and water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH). With FY 2022 funds, the activity will focus primarily on addressing the FP needs of Ghanaian individuals, couples and families by deploying a robust commodity distribution strategy and supporting it with innovative interventions to reach the most rural communities. The activity will increase the demand for these products through a social and behavioral change communication campaign that promotes modern contraceptives and addresses individuals' desire to avoid unintended pregnancies. TFHO will socially market water purification tablets in hard-to-reach communities without potable drinking water until these communities are provided with more robust and sustainable clean potable drinking water interventions. TFHO will work closely with Ghana Health Service and private health facilities to ensure compliance with national treatment guidelines on use of chlorhexidine gel for umbilical cord care in newborns and strategically introduce clean delivery kits for mothers during delivery where most needed.This Activity will also work with the Enhancing WASH Activity to identify sources of supplies for menstrual hygiene products (both reusable and disposable) and develop a social marketing brand for commercial introduction. In addition, it will work with stakeholders to develop sustainable markets for sanitation products e.g. SaTo pan, Digniloo, and other sanitation-related products across the country. In addition, USAID will strengthen the technical, organizational, and fiscal capacity of this new local organization and ensure sustained social marketing of health products.
